The proof separates the largest proper divisor from an exponentially smaller remainder. We also prove Bala's generating functions and prime congruences, and give an explicit proof of Kotešovec's previously recorded Fibonacci-transform asymptotic.

works.abstract_text: We prove Paul Curtz's six-residue denominator conjecture in OEIS A189733, revision 12, COMMENTS (May 23, 2011), now in revision 36, FORMULA, with its convention that zero has denominator one. Following Gao's earlier generating-function proof, we derive exact values of the first row of the defining rational array. These values also prove the six-periodic numerator assertion, the denominator recurrence, and Barker's empirical generating function in the same entry. The same formulas settle Barker's recurrence and generating-function conjectures in A267068 and give the numerator identities in A278718. We also prove the full-array reflection and binomial-transform identity. The corresponding second-kind array yields A194767's denominator formulas and reciprocal sum, and corrects an index in its fourth-diagonal numerator identity. For the unsigned-seed array in A189731 and A242926, the same argument gives a Lucas-number formula and refutes the asserted prime-only integer ranks at the composite 705. An integer triangular transformation determines antidiagonal denominator lcms for arbitrary rational seeds.

For every real t >= 1 and positive integer n, let u be the largest divisor of n whose consecutive divisors have ratio at most t. Each maximal t-dense block of divisors of n is a disjoint union of complete copies of D(u), scaled by divisors of n/u. The proof uses the classical dense/rough divisor decomposition and an elementary argument that a dense copy cannot cross a block boundary.

For arbitrary finite-alphabet gates, a perfect six-leg composite forces perfect factors. Six specified permutation flattenings characterize this property. A norm–determinant argument gives the quantum analogue for unitary gates, extending the prior forward construction of §3.2, Theorems 1–2. For arbitrary complex factors, the same six unitary exterior flattenings guarantee perfect replacement tensors at the same bond dimension. works.abstract_text: Question 2.32 on page 14 of Remi Salinas Schmeis's General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into ω-Chains (arXiv:2610.29056v1, 2026) asks whether every poset has an ω-chain-partitionable extension that order-embeds into every such extension. We answer negatively: even a two-element antichain has no such extension. Two countable extensions force incompatible behavior for upper bounds of incomparable elements. The same argument gives the connected three-element fork as a counterexample and, by order duality, the corresponding negative answer for ω*-chains. More generally, a nonempty countable poset of bounded finite height has such a least extension if and only if it has a greatest element. Every poset has a partitionable extension, even with ω replaced by any nonzero ordinal.

works.abstract_text: For Sun's On some determinants with Legendre symbol entries, arXiv:1308.2900v5, Conjecture 3.16, p. 17, we extend the zero-class identity credited to C. Krattenthaler in arXiv:1308.2900v6 (April 24, 2014), Remark 3.16. For A006077, the Hankel determinant of order n+1 vanishes exactly when n is congruent to 1 modulo 3; otherwise its quotient by (-1)^floor((n+1)/3) 6^n is a positive odd integer. Binomial translation gives a three-block factorization. Integral row normalization reduces parity to the Rueppel determinants, and a positive moment representation gives the sign. We also give parameter-independent and square-class consequences, the exact inertia, and a two-parameter deformation. Related moment arguments establish the harmonic sign assertion in Conjecture 3.9(i) and the two squared-number assertions in Conjecture 3.17.

works.abstract_text: We answer negatively Ta's Problems 11.6–11.7 in arXiv:2505.08090v5, Section 11, page 27, and prove his Conjecture 5.13 in arXiv:2508.16772v1, Section 5.2.2, page 17, extending the counting methods of Kamada–Oshiro (2009), Ta (2025), and Nakajima–Yamaguchi (2026). The two semidirect products C16 semidirect C4 with actions 5 and 7 have invariant triple (64,4,22), but respectively 8847360 and 2160000 good involutions. Ta's central-label characterization gives a weighted-involution formula for every finite conjugation subquandle and an exact criterion for equality in the central-label bound. The quaternion example attains that bound with two orbits and a center of order two. Inversion-closure is distinguished from classwise inverse stability, correcting Remark 2.14. For the linear quandle Lambda_(4n,2n-1), the number of good involutions is ten for odd n and four for even n; the odd case proves Conjecture 5.13, and the even case reproves Ta's Remark 5.14.

works.abstract_text: Ta's Problem 11.7 (arXiv:2505.08090v5, p. 27) has answer no: extending the dihedral examples of Kamada and Oshiro (2009/2010), we characterize equality in the center term of the good-involution bound. For finite H generated by a conjugation subquandle X with |Z(H)|>=2, equality holds exactly when z O^{-1}=O for every central z and every H-conjugation orbit O. The criterion gives equality examples in Q8^d with center order 2^d, 3^d orbits and 2^(d*3^d) good involutions. Reflection families rederive the known good-involution counts, affine antiautomorphism group and symmetric-isomorphism classes. Inverse-closure permutes, rather than necessarily fixes, conjugation orbits, correcting Ta's Remark 2.14.

works.abstract_text: The Shannon conjecture following Eq. (69) in Section V.C of Tarabunga et al., arXiv:2411.05766v1, is false. An explicit three-qubit state has stabilizer-basis entropy log 4, whereas the proposed absolute-amplitude lower bound is log 16 - (9/8) log 3 > log 4. The same construction refutes the bound for nonnegative amplitudes, and continuity gives strictly positive examples. It extends to every N >= 3 and to a range of Renyi indices containing one. The collision entropy of the comparison distribution remains a valid Shannon lower bound for arbitrary affine supports. For amplitudes of constant modulus on each affine coset, the original bound holds at every Renyi index; this includes the source's Figure 1 product states.

For the logarithmic coefficient array A(n,k), every prime column has residue -1, and k divides A(n,k) holds exactly for nonprime k >= 1, apart from k = 4, whose residue is always 2. The quotient A(n,p)/(p-1) is integral and congruent to 1 modulo p for every even row; evenness is necessary only at p = 3,5. A factorial coefficient expansion also gives fixed-row recurrences, asymptotics, and an integer-parameter extension.

works.abstract_text: We resolve User3's question (question 515549, revision 1, September 25, 2026): for every nonsingular real square matrix of positive size, the orthogonal minimum of rho(|PQ||Q^T P^{-1}|) is attained and equals one. Thus the proposed strict uniform lower bound cannot hold for any such matrix. We give a self-contained exposition of the triangularization proof in the pinned formal source, then characterize every minimizer by independent row and column permutations to triangular form. For fixed P, the set of minimizers is finite and has an explicit description using row-permuted QR factorizations. The same minimum holds over the special orthogonal group. Finally, the companion absolute-row-sum balancing question follows from the Yamabe-Yujobo theorem.

works.abstract_text: We answer the realizability question of Vélez Caicedo and Cadavid (§5, p. 17, second paragraph of arXiv:2611.14316v1) by reflecting semigroup generators about a prescribed maximum jump: every numerical semigroup T is realizable, and a positive integer M is an admissible maximum exactly when M belongs to T and every minimal generator h satisfies h<2M and 2M-h belongs to T. The construction gives the unique inclusion-minimal jump set at each admissible maximum and realizes every sufficiently large maximum. Using the source's spectral formulas, we also recover the semigroup from two global dimensions and M-2 restricted dimensions when M>=2. For prime maxima, eventual dimensions at proper-divisor moduli alone need not distinguish semigroups.

works.abstract_text: For Chakrabarty and Kundu, arXiv:2610.35838v1 (2026), Section III D, page 5, Table III and Eq. (15), we complete the W-state and generalized-GHZ Bell-measurement optimizations and recover the W single-node value from Horodecki et al. (1995). The W-state value is exactly sqrt(13)/3. We prove the upper bound over both central orthonormal frames and every parity-index pair, including identity indices and repeated pairs. A quadratic identity for the W correlation tensor reduces the proof to Parseval's identity and a two-by-two submatrix estimate. Consequently the white-noise threshold in this measurement class is exactly 3/sqrt(13); ignoring either central node gives 2*sqrt(2)/3. An ellipsoid bound gives N_c(GHZ_alpha)=sqrt(1+sin^2(2alpha)), settling the neighboring conjecture. We also give the unequal-visibility threshold and explicit W-state entanglement-swapping probabilities.

works.abstract_text: We refute Conjectures 3.26 and 5.3 of Wang's Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups (arXiv:2509.18724v1, pp. 23 and 27). The commutative periodic monoid of finite subsets of the natural numbers, paired with levels zero, one and two under union and capped addition, has algebraic Davenport constant one over every nonzero commutative unitary ring. Its nongroup relative Davenport constants are unbounded. The finite submonoids with supports contained in {1,...,m}, m>=1, have the same algebraic constant, whereas the expression conjectured to equal it grows without bound as m increases.

An injection sends a partition with nonnegative reverse-alternating sum to an odd-length partition of the next weight. We characterize equality, give an explicit lower bound for the deficit, and deduce monotonicity of the corresponding unrestricted count. The same parity analysis proves a shifted companion comparison, determines all plateaus of the negative-sum count, and corrects neighboring indexing and distinct-part descriptions. A bivariate series settles the linked ordered-composition interpretations, with their precise shifts.

works.abstract_text: The question in Xu et al., Section 4.2, page 12 of arXiv:2211.05563v1, asks whether the optimized witness bound equals the convex-roof geometric measure of genuine multipartite entanglement for noisy GHZ states. A strict separation holds for every party count n >= 3 and local dimension d >= 3 at an explicit noise probability. For three qutrits at noise p=3/8, the optimized witness bound is exactly 1/9, whereas the convex roof is at least 13/108. A biseparable overlap inequality and a positive-definite matrix give a two-observable lower bound. A written corollary extends the three-qutrit strict gap throughout 27/74 < p < 9/22.

works.abstract_text: Extending the two-sided destruction construction of Saxena, Chitambar and Gour (2019), we answer Yoeli and Gour's fixed-superchannel question in Instability as a Quantum Resource, arXiv:2602.18323v1, p. 5, Open directions, negatively: in every dimension d >= 3, dephasing-covariant channels are not exactly the fixed channels of any deterministic superchannel. Any completely positive Choi action fixing every such channel must be the identity. Two-sector pinching, including qubit complete dephasing, admits an explicit physical projection. Uniformity-preserving channels have the same obstruction in every dimension d >= 2. Explicit negative determinants distinguish linear projection from physical retraction and give a counterexample to the affine-set assertion in arXiv:2402.05474v2, Theorem 9.2.

works.abstract_text: For Zhan–Gupta–Hillery, Section 5, Conjecture 2 (2024, p. 10:11; arXiv:2306.17401v6, p. 11), we derive a strict-averaging counterexample from the complementary-layer Gram formula of Skotiniotis et al. (2018). Two different coefficient-square distributions and their whole averaging segment have the same Gram matrix and, for three sensors at theta = pi/4, the same error (14 - 4*sqrt(10))/27. We extend the earlier symmetric-probe calculation by proving weak convexity and the existence of a symmetric pure optimum without a symmetry assumption. This proves the companion Conjecture 1 and answers the source’s final question: one probe is optimal for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination at every detector angle. The reductions also apply to fixed unequal priors and diagonal impact patterns, without solving their general optimizers.
